# Vendored PouchDB test files

Spec 03 task 1 decision: vendor real spec files from `apache/pouchdb`'s
`tests/integration/` rather than write a bespoke suite. PouchDB doesn't publish an
installable conformance package, and third-party adapters that get its suite "for
free" (e.g. `pouchdb-adapter-fs`) all do so by building on
`pouchdb-adapter-leveldb-core` — a key/value seam. This adapter deliberately isn't
that (ADR-0001: document-level seam, no leveldown interface), so there's no
off-the-shelf path; vendoring real upstream files is the most faithful alternative to
spec 03's "PouchDB's adapter conformance suite passes in full."

Every vendored file's `adapters` array must be trimmed to `['local']` — there is no
CouchDB `http` target in this project.

| File | Vendored from | Modifications |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `test.aa.setup.js` | `apache/pouchdb`, `master`, `tests/integration/test.aa.setup.js` (fetched 2026-08-09) | `require('../../packages/node_modules/pouchdb/package.json')` → `require('pouchdb-core/package.json')` — the upstream path only resolves inside the pouchdb monorepo; we depend on `pouchdb-core` directly, not the `pouchdb` meta-package. |
| `test.local_docs.js` | `apache/pouchdb`, `master`, `tests/integration/test.local_docs.js` (fetched 2026-08-09) | `adapters` trimmed from `['http', 'local']` to `['local']` only, per the rule above. No other changes — passes as-is against `_getLocal`/`_putLocal`/`_removeLocal` (spec 03 task 2), including the `"0-N"`/`"0-0"` rev format and conflict-detection semantics this task added to the `putLocal`/`removeLocal` native contract specifically to make this file pass unmodified. |
| `test.bulk_docs.js` | `apache/pouchdb`, `master`, `tests/integration/test.bulk_docs.js` (fetched 2026-08-09) | `adapters` trimmed to `['local']`. `test/testUtils.js` grew `errors` (re-exports `pouchdb-errors`, the real package this adapter already depends on), `rev` (from `pouchdb-utils`, matching upstream's own `pouchUtils.rev` — see below), and stub `isCouchDB`/`isSafari`/`isCouchMaster` (always false/`cb(false)` — this project never runs against a real CouchDB or in a browser, but the vendored file still calls these directly). 12 cases skipped, each annotated in-file: 9 need `_allDocs`/`_changes` (spec 03 task 4 — two of the nine surface as a mocha timeout rather than a clean failure, since their callback-style call sites don't check `err` before touching the unavailable result, and PouchDB's own promise chain swallows the resulting throw as an unhandled rejection instead of failing the test); 2 need active old-revision-body deletion once past `revs_limit`, not just tree stemming (`4204 respect revs_limit`, the tree-only case, already passes) — that's compaction, spec 03 task 7. Vendoring this file surfaced a real native-contract gap: two concurrent `_bulkDocs` calls to the same brand-new doc id both succeeded silently (no conflict) because `bulkWrite` unconditionally overwrote whatever was stored, with nothing checking that the tree JS merged against was still current (`handles simultaneous writes`). Fixed across all three repos by adding `WriteOp.expectedPrevWinningRev` (a compare-and-swap token, not a tree-semantics decision — ADR-0001 still holds) that `bulkWrite` checks per op, rejecting (not batch-failing) any op whose assumption has gone stale; see `specs/02-docstack-store.md`. |
| `test.basics.js` | `apache/pouchdb`, `master`, `tests/integration/test.basics.js` (fetched 2026-08-09) | `adapters` trimmed to `['local']`. 21 cases skipped, each annotated in-file: 8 need `_destroy`, 5 need `_close` (spec 03 task 7); 7 need `_allDocs`/`_changes`, including two "Fail to fetch a doc..." variants and one whose callback-style call site turns the not-implemented error into a mocha timeout, same pattern as `test.bulk_docs.js` (spec 03 task 4); 2 need the `pouchdb-replication` plugin (`db.replicate`), which this harness never loads — out of scope for a local-only adapter, not a gap; 1 (`putting is override-able`) can't pass under any adapter as written — it calls `db.put(doc)` with no trailing callback and then asserts a monkey-patched `put` saw one, a legacy `initPull`/`cleanupPut` replication-hook pattern `pouchdb-core@9` doesn't wire up this way anymore. Vendoring this file surfaced two more real gaps, both fixed across all repos: `info().doc_count` counted every doc regardless of deletion (`db.info should give correct doc_count`) instead of excluding docs whose winning revision is deleted, per CouchDB's own semantics — fixed in `InMemoryDocumentStore`, `RocksDbDocumentStore`, and the fake carrier; and `db.id()` had no adapter method at all (`this._id` was simply never assigned, not even stubbed, causing `db.id()` to hang rather than fail) — added `_id`, backed by a reserved `_local/instanceId` local doc reusing the existing `putLocal`/`getLocal` primitives, same pattern the reference `pouchdb-adapter-leveldb-core` uses (a persisted-UUID metadata key), just riding the local-doc contract instead of a bespoke one. |
| `test.get.js` | `apache/pouchdb`, `master`, `tests/integration/test.get.js` (fetched 2026-08-09) | `adapters` trimmed to `['local']`. `test/testUtils.js` grew `putAfter`/`putBranch`/`putTree`/`writeDocs`, ported verbatim from upstream's `utils.js` (needed to build synthetic rev trees for conflict/branch tests) — this is what pulled `pouchdb-utils` from a test-only devDependency into a real production `dependencies` entry, since `_id` (added while triaging `test.basics.js`, see above) also needs `pouchdb-utils`'s `uuid()`. 7 cases skipped, all the `5857 - ... latest=true` family — `_get`'s `latest` option (resolve to a branch's current leaf instead of the literal requested rev) was already explicitly deferred in `src/index.ts`'s `_get` doc comment back in spec 03 task 2 ("`revs`/`open_revs`/`conflicts` options need real multi-revision trees to mean anything and are follow-up work"); vendoring this file just gave that deferral concrete failing test cases, not a new discovery. |

Files land here as the adapter methods they exercise are implemented (spec 03 tasks
2+), not all at once — task 1 only proves the harness runs a real upstream file at
all.
